title: Matthias Corvinus to Ercole I d'Este, Pozsony, 1 June 1482, ASMo CPE 1622 b. 1/3 nos. 2, 2a (DECODE R1156)

documents.shelfmark: Modena, Archivio di Stato, Cancelleria, Carteggio principi esteri 1622, b. 1/3, nos. 2, 2a (DECODE R1156)

plaintext.source: Magyar diplomacziai emlekek III (1877) no. 14; Fraknoi, Matyas kiraly levelei II (1895) no. 131, pp. 232-233, from the original (fraknoi_v2.txt)

transcription.source: DECODE images I5815 (letter) and I5816 (verso, address and seal), login required
transcription.notes: About 15 cipher runs, 'roughly 330 signs' per NOTES; no sign-by-sign ciphertext file was saved, so the count is not measured. The runs are given word by word with their readings in NOTES.

system.summary: Letter substitution in invented graphic signs with homophones for the common letters, plus three name signs (Venetians, King Ferdinand, Matthias).
system.doubled_letters: special sign: a sign between dots (tt)
system.notes: Working key from the NOTES table; some signs do double duty (+ as o, t and e; 2 as i and d), and the sample is too short to split them, so per_letter counts are of the table, not a clean key.

prior_solution.where: Magyar diplomacziai emlekek III (1877) no. 14; Fraknoi 1895 no. 131. DECODE 'partially decrypted' only means no transcription was entered.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session token to the model (decode/jwt.txt, git-ignored), set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the pre-1497 candidate list. No target-specific intervention recorded in NOTES or git.

solution.what: DECODE record R1156 and its two images fetched with a login.
Found the letter printed in full in MDE III (1877) no. 14 and Fraknoi II (1895) no. 131, from the Modena original.
Working key rebuilt from the cipher runs aligned with the printed text, each value checked on at least two words; three name signs identified.

Every run read from the glyphs; four corrections to the print (valent, gentibus, the closing 'Speramus cito nos res nostras ita disposituros...', and the 'contemporary regest' shown to be the letter's own half-ciphered last sentence).
'illic faciet [q-sign] venient' against printed 'convenire', and two signs after 'regina' on line 3, left unresolved.

outcome.method_basis: The letter was printed in full in Magyar diplomacziai emlekek III (1877) no. 14 and Fraknoi 1895 no. 131 from the Modena original; a working key was rebuilt here by aligning the cipher runs with the print and every run re-read from the glyphs, correcting four passages of the print.
outcome.fraction_read_source: NOTES.md: about 330 signs (NOTES estimate), of which the 2 signs after 'regina' are unread
outcome.notes: Printed 1877/1895; re-read here from the glyphs with four corrections to the print. NOTES Status says 'read'; the README lists it under 'Found already solved by others', which this class follows. codes_open counts the three identified name signs plus the two unread signs after 'regina' as 5 (the README row calls those two 'name signs'; NOTES only '2 signs').
